lines.text: In Ghana, there is a phrase every emergency worker knows.
lines.say: In Ghana, there is a phrase every emergency worker knows.

lines.text: No bed syndrome.
lines.say: No bed syndrome.

lines.text: On the 6th of February 2026, Charles Amissah, a 29-year-old engineer, was hit by a car at the Circle overpass in Accra.
lines.say: On the sixth of February, twenty twenty-six, Charles Amissah, a twenty-nine year old engineer, was hit by a car at the Circle overpass in Accra.

lines.text: Paramedics reached him and stabilised him.
lines.say: Paramedics reached him, and stabilised him.

lines.text: Then the ambulance went to the Police Hospital.
lines.say: Then the ambulance went to the Police Hospital.

lines.text: Then to Ridge Hospital.
lines.say: Then to Ridge Hospital.

lines.text: Then to Korle Bu.
lines.say: Then to Korlay Boo.

lines.text: Each time, the answer was the same: no bed.
lines.say: Each time, the answer was the same. No bed.

lines.text: A Ministry of Health committee later described a 118-minute referral loop. He did not survive.
lines.say: A Ministry of Health committee later described a one hundred and eighteen minute referral loop. He did not survive.

lines.text: His story is not rare.
lines.say: His story is not rare.

lines.text: Ghana has fewer than one hospital bed for every 1,000 people: about 0.7 to 0.9.
lines.say: Ghana has fewer than one hospital bed for every thousand people. About zero point seven, to zero point nine.

lines.text: Major hospitals report running at 120 to 150 percent of their capacity.
lines.say: Major hospitals report running at one hundred and twenty, to one hundred and fifty percent of their capacity.

lines.text: And in mid-2025, Greater Accra, a region of over five million people, had only about 42 ambulances available.
lines.say: And in mid twenty twenty-five, Greater Accra, a region of over five million people, had only about forty-two ambulances available.

lines.text: But beds are only part of the problem. The deeper failure is information.
lines.say: But beds are only part of the problem. The deeper failure is information.

lines.text: When an ambulance leaves the scene, nobody knows which hospital has a free bed.
lines.say: When an ambulance leaves the scene, nobody knows which hospital has a free bed.

lines.text: Crews find out by driving there. Every wrong stop costs minutes a patient may not have.
lines.say: Crews find out by driving there. Every wrong stop costs minutes a patient may not have.

lines.text: That is why we are building BedAlert: a live, shared view of free hospital beds across Ghana.
lines.say: That is why we are building Bed Alert. A live, shared view of free hospital beds across Ghana.

lines.text: Hospitals update their free beds with one tap, or connect their own systems so the numbers update automatically.
lines.say: Hospitals update their free beds with one tap, or connect their own systems, so the numbers update automatically.

lines.text: Ambulance dispatchers see the nearest hospital with a confirmed free bed, and hold it before the ambulance moves.
lines.say: Ambulance dispatchers see the nearest hospital with a confirmed free bed, and hold it before the ambulance moves.

lines.text: If a hospital declines, BedAlert immediately holds a bed at the next one.
lines.say: If a hospital declines, Bed Alert immediately holds a bed at the next one.

lines.text: Families can find and hold a bed from a phone browser.
lines.say: Families can find and hold a bed from a phone browser.

lines.text: And people without smartphones or data can dial a USSD code, and get their confirmation by SMS.
lines.say: And people without smartphones or data can dial a U S S D code, and get their confirmation by S M S.

lines.text: A held bed is released automatically if the patient doesn't arrive, so beds are never locked away.
lines.say: A held bed is released automatically if the patient doesn't arrive, so beds are never locked away.

lines.text: Out-of-date numbers are flagged, not hidden. And BedAlert shares bed counts, never patient records.
lines.say: Out of date numbers are flagged, not hidden. And Bed Alert shares bed counts, never patient records.

lines.text: The core system is already built and tested.
lines.say: The core system is already built and tested.

lines.text: Next: the hospital, dispatcher and citizen apps, real SMS and USSD, and a pilot with hospitals and an ambulance station in one district.
lines.say: Next, the hospital, dispatcher and citizen apps, real S M S and U S S D, and a pilot with hospitals and an ambulance station in one district.

lines.text: We are looking for partner hospitals, the National Ambulance Service, and health leaders ready to end no bed syndrome.
lines.say: We are looking for partner hospitals, the National Ambulance Service, and health leaders ready to end no bed syndrome.

lines.text: No patient should die looking for a bed.
lines.say: No patient should die looking for a bed.

lines.text: BedAlert was started by Robert Hasford, Biomedical Engineering at KNUST, with Jayne and Welam, Medical Laboratory Science at the University of Ghana.
lines.say: Bed Alert was started by Robert Hasford, biomedical engineering at K N U S T, together with Jayne and Welam, medical laboratory science at the University of Ghana.
